title: NASP as cover program for Aurora
summary: Nick Cook tells of NASP as cover program for Aurora, about 1980s-1990s at United States (no place named), and relays what a named person told them. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: And Bill became convinced that NASP was actually a cover program for Aurora.

plain: Nick Cook, an aviation journalist, passes on a suspicion held by a fellow aviation writer, Bill Sweetman, about secret American aircraft in the 1980s and 1990s. According to Cook, Sweetman came to believe that NASP, a public US government project to build a plane that could fly into space, was really a cover for Aurora, a rumoured secret high-speed aircraft. If so, a project the public could see would have been hiding a far more advanced one they couldn't.
